newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Germany's HDI group acquires Brazilian insurer.
newsitem.headline: Germany's HDI group acquires Brazilian insurer.

text.p: Germany's Euro-Hannover Holding N.V., a unit of HDI group, said it has fully acquired Brazilian insurance firm Hannover Paulista Seguros by buying the remaining 50 percent voting stake in the local insurer.
The company would not disclose how much it paid for the stake.
HDI group plans to invest five million marks in Hannover Paulista Seguros, a private firm, to develop new insurance plans for companies and individuals, the company said in a statement.

"HDI group always believed in the potential of the Brazilian (insurance) market and now, with economic stability, we believe even more," said Hendrick Jan Van der Hoeven, president of Euro-Hannover Holding N.V.
Hoeven said the company plans to launch in Brazil a new product called Hannover Personal which will offer coverage for personal injury and theft or damage to objects in one policy.
Hannover Paulista Seguros was a joint-venture between Brazilian insurer Paulista Seguros and HDI group.

Paulista Seguros decided to sell its 50 percent voting stake in Hannover Paulista Seguros because last year it set a partnership with U.S. insurance firm Liberty Mutual to provide insurance services in Brazil.

Hannover Paulista Seguros posted a net profit of 800,000 reais ($764,380) last year, with revenues soaring 65 percent to 55 million reais. This year the company expects revenues to reach 70 million reais.
Foreign insurers are flocking to Brazil to snap up local firms to gain a foothold in a market that is expected to grow 15 percent annually over the next decade.
